title: [Feature Request] Auto-detect nearest cut point when adding transitions (no clip selection required)
summary: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Applying transitions currently requires too much manual targeting—either needing to select/box-select both adjacent clips or dragging the transition with extreme precision onto the tiny seam between clips. When editing fast-paced montages with dozens of cuts, this extra friction quickly becomes tedious and slows down timeline workflows. **Describe the solution you'd like** - **Smart Cut Detection**: When dragging a transition near a cut point (or double-clicking a transition preset), the timeline should automatically detect and snap to the nearest split/seam between two clips on the active track. - **No Multi-Selection Needed**: Users should not need to highlight or select both adjacent clips beforehand just to place a transition between them. - **Magnetic Snapping**: Provide a generous snapping radius so dragging a transition anywhere close to a boundary effortlessly locks it into place. **Describe alternatives you've considered** - **Manual clip multi-selection (Shift + Click both clips)**: Too many unnecessary clicks for a basic repetitive task. - **Precision drag-and-drop**: Frustrating on high-DPI displays or zoomed-out timelines where cut boundaries are only a few pixels wide. **Additional context** Most modern editors (such as CapCut or Premiere Pro) auto-target the nearest edit point or provide clickable transition placeholders directly between cut clips. Implementing this smart snapping would make pacing and transition workflows vastly more intuitive.
